# Palliative and advance care planning in PD — facts

> Source-anchored units about Palliative and advance care planning in PD: 16 across 2 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

## Structure and components

- [statement] Advance care planning includes clarifying values, choosing a surrogate, discussing future medical care and documenting preferences; paperwork is one part of the process. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6556088/ · keywords: Palliative and advance care planning in PD · also: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations

## How it works

- [statement] Advance care planning is a continuing discussion of future care needs, wishes and preferences, including decisions for a time when a person may be unable to decide independently. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8355553/ · keywords: Palliative and advance care planning in PD · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13771020/
- [statement] Individual readiness and timing matter: interview findings support regularly revisiting information preferences, while the PD_Pal contextual analysis found both resistance when discussion felt premature and cognitive limitations that could obstruct later participation. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8355553/ · keywords: Palliative and advance care planning in PD · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13771020/
- [statement] PD_Pal’s authors identify fragmented electronic-record documentation and limited visibility as possible reasons recorded preferences may be missed; documentation alone may not capture the quality or process of ACP discussions. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13771020/ · keywords: Palliative and advance care planning in PD

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The 2020 randomized trial enrolled 210 people with PD or related disorders with moderate-to-high palliative needs; at 6 months the palliative-care group had better quality of life (treatment effect 1.87; 95% CI 0.47–3.27). Its mixed diagnostic population and selected needs limit extrapolation to all PD patients. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7042842/ · keywords: Palliative and advance care planning in PD
- [statement] The 2020 trial found improved advance-directive completion among secondary outcomes, but its lack of demographic diversity and conduct at experienced academic centers limit generalizability. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7042842/ · keywords: Palliative and advance care planning in PD

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Lum and colleagues recommend starting ACP discussions early because later communication and cognitive difficulties can reduce participation; they also recommend checking readiness, knowledge and information needs rather than assuming everyone wants the same discussion. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6556088/ · keywords: Palliative and advance care planning in PD
- [statement] In that 2020 trial, among participants without an advance directive at baseline, six-month completion was 53% with palliative care versus 26% with standard care; the health-care-proxy completion comparison was not significant. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7042842/ · keywords: Palliative and advance care planning in PD
- [statement] In the 2021 qualitative interview study of 20 patients, most wanted ACP discussion with a clinician and the majority preferred clinician initiation early in the disease; preferred information timing varied. These are participant perspectives rather than evidence that everyone wants immediate detailed end-of-life planning. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8355553/ · keywords: Palliative and advance care planning in PD

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Palliative care addresses symptoms, psychosocial concerns and future planning; NICE recommends considering referral at any stage of PD, so it need not wait until the terminal phase. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7042842/ · keywords: Palliative and advance care planning in PD · also: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations
- [statement] NICE’s 2017 PD recommendations advise oral and written information about progression, future treatment options and end-of-life issues, with the discussion recorded; named UK planning mechanisms include ADRT, DNACPR and Lasting Power of Attorney. These are UK guideline examples, not universal legal instruments. (low confidence) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Palliative and advance care planning in PD
- [statement] In the 2026 PD_Pal trial, 189 participants with advanced parkinsonism were randomized to a six-month nurse-led ACP and care-coordination intervention or usual care; documented end-of-life preferences did not differ significantly at six months (P=0.77). This trial does not establish that structured ACP universally improves documentation. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13771020/ · keywords: Palliative and advance care planning in PD
- [statement] Benefits in one palliative-care trial should not be generalized to every ACP intervention: the 2020 intervention improved advance-directive completion, whereas PD_Pal in 2026 did not improve its primary documentation endpoint. They tested different interventions and populations. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7042842/ · keywords: Palliative and advance care planning in PD · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13771020/
- [statement] The 2020 trial did not demonstrate a significant between-group reduction in healthcare use; the authors cautioned that relevant events were few. Reduced hospitalization should not be presented as an established result of that trial. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7042842/ · keywords: Palliative and advance care planning in PD
- [statement] Generalizability of the 2020 trial is limited by experienced academic sites, a population lacking diversity and an unblinded design with possible patient-reported-outcome bias. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7042842/ · keywords: Palliative and advance care planning in PD
- [statement] NICE recommends prognosis discussions that promote patient priorities and shared decisions, and recognition that relatives may have different information needs from the person with PD. (low confidence) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Palliative and advance care planning in PD
